findings: - blocking: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:14-15` — `MarketingLayout` reads `navCache` (a module-level `Map`), but only `generateStaticParams` fills it. Next.js does not promise that this function runs in the same process or worker that renders the layout. A cold server start, an ISR (incremental regeneration) or dynamic render, and dev mode all begin with an empty cache. When the cache is empty, `if (!nav) return null` drops the whole shell and `children` too. Users and crawlers then get a blank page, which breaks the user flow. Fix: fetch the nav inside the layout itself, for example `await fetch(..., { next: { revalidate } })`.

- blocking: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:7-11` — `generateStaticParams` returns `{ segment }`, but the `app/(marketing)/` path has no dynamic segment such as `[segment]`. `(marketing)` is only a route group — a folder name that does not appear in the URL. The params therefore do not apply. Since the cache fill also depends on this function running, the layout's data source is not reliable. This is a server rendering boundary break.

- suggestion: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:29-31` — returning `null` makes a failed nav fetch hide the page body as well. A better fallback is to always render `<main>{children}</main>` and leave out only the nav.
- suggestion: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:8-9` — the code does not check `response.ok`. A CMS error body would be stored as `NavItem[]`, and `nav.map` would then fail at render time.

- blocking: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:7-11` — `generateStaticParams` fills the module-level `navCache` as a side effect. It runs at build time, in a separate worker/process from rendering, and is not a data-loading hook. When `MarketingLayout` renders, `navCache.get('marketing')` can be `undefined`. The layout then returns `null` and blanks every marketing page, which breaks both the user flow and the server rendering boundary.

- blocking: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:15` — `if (!nav) return null` drops `children` too, not just the nav. One CMS miss removes the whole page body, the `<main>` and the footer, from the server HTML. Users and crawlers get an empty document. Render `children` in the shell no matter what, and treat a missing nav as an empty or error state.

- blocking: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:10` — `(marketing)` is a route group with no dynamic segment, so the returned `{ segment: ... }` params match no route param. This `generateStaticParams` cannot produce the `home`/`pricing` pages it lists. The build fails or silently ignores it, and nothing reliably fills the cache.

- suggestion: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:5` — A module-level `Map` in a Server Component is process-global state shared across requests. It also never refreshes. Fetch the nav inside the async layout with `await fetch(...)` and use Next.js caching/revalidation instead.
- suggestion: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:8-9` — The code never checks `response.ok` or the response shape. A CMS error body would be cached as `NavItem[]`, and `nav.map` would throw during render.
- suggestion: `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx:23,31` — Internal links use plain `<a>` instead of `next/link`, so every nav click reloads the whole page. This only matters if the repo already uses `Link`.
